cs.th: Samsung Unveils 15.6-Inch Ultra-HD OLED Display for Laptops

cs.t: My own experience doesn't match yours. I've bought 6 XPS laptops and a couple of desktops (including Alienware) over the last 20 years and have had a pretty good experience with all of them. They always had nice screens, good performance, and held up to the stresses and strains of travel and heavy usage. That doesn't mean I haven't had a handful of issues, such as several swollen batteries that caused problemss with the touch pad and keyboard. But Dell fixed the ones (onsite!) that occurred during the warranty period and I was able to fix the ones that occurred outside the warranty period. The only issue that really sticks with me is one I had with motherboard fan controls (not lights, but fan speed) in an Alienware R6 that could only be engaged and adjusted via Windows software. Thanks to proprietary Dell bios shenanigans I couldn't get control of the fan via Linux no matter what I tried. That said, I don't find this "Create Edition" model appealing for so many of the reasons other posters have pointed out (price, Windows preinstalled, etc.). And I really dislike monitors that use uncommon resolutions (I think this one is 3200x2000).

This is basically my experience. I switched to Mac with the Intel change around...2006 maybe? Converted my entire family. I personally switched to various flavors of linux around 2016-2017 because I wanted more hardware options. Eventually, my son got into gaming and eventually we let him get an Alienware laptop maybe 2-3 years ago. Then my wife had to get one for work this year. It's like nothing has improved in 20 years.

cs.t: I've used 4k TVs and currently a UWHD (Dell AW3420DW) If you have a good enough monitor for gaming already and are more interested in programming aspect, I'd def recommend a 37-42" 4K tv. Way more for your buck. If you can find a TV with 120Hz refresh, that would be sufficient for gaming too. One thing to note is that ultrawides are not great for full screen sharing as everyone else pretty much uses a different aspect ratio.
cs.th: Ask HN: Best ultrawide monitor for programming and gaming?

cs.t: I currently work on an Alienware 15 and it is sweet. Two requirements I had were:  (i) NVIDIA 10-series discrete graphics,  and (2) 32MB of RAM.  I wasn't excited about the 4K display until I saw it,  now I am never going back.  Also the build quality is great. Apple backed the wrong horse in the GPU wars a few years back,  I think all of their machines still ship with ATI GPUs if the have a discrete GPU.  I think for gaming and creative work ATI is OK but if you do neural networks or other heavy calculations software support is not universal for tools like Tensorflow, Torch,  etc. as it is for NVIDIA. Most of the time I would also tell you that you can get a lot more computer for your $ and not be complaining about drivers for your OS or you don't like the ports by getting a desktop machine. I recently bought a tower machine built from refurb parts,  put in 32MB of RAM and a GTX 1050 graphics card (largest that wouldn't need special considerations for power supply) for a machine that I mainly use as a media server but may also want to run some Tensorflow.  What I paid for the 1050 card was crazy because the price has been driven up by bitcoiners. My only bitch about ML on a laptop is that it is not necessarily the kind of thing you want to do on a machine where you close the lid.  For instance on evening I closed the lid when the system was uploading a model to a server and the server never got it...
cs.th: Ask HN: What is the best laptop for programming/data science?
